#1455. Karl-Heinz Rummenigge’s heavy statements on Jamal Musiala divide Bayern more than ever

“What we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level he has so often displayed here. We need to talk to the family, the player and especially his representatives. These sums are no longer possible – sorry, with all due respect.» Karl-Heinz Rummenigge opened Pandora’s box last night. After the draw against Cologne where the German champion lost Harry Kane for three months and Michael Olise for a few weeks, the member of the supervisory board, and former chairman of the club’s board of directors, hit hard on the young attacking midfielder.

The latter suffers from a neurological dysfunction which prevents him from being able to take part in high-level meetings. Despite a treatment protocol and an illness that is not serious, the attacking midfielder is subject to dizziness on the field. He even passes out sometimes. The problem has been known to Bayern for a long time and until recent months seemed rather controllable. For some time now, Musiala has experienced several discomforts in matches and training. His level of performance is no longer the same and his case necessarily raises questions. He is one of Bayern’s highest paid players.

Rummenigge thinks above all about the future of the club. If he wants Musiala to return, the former striker, now 71 years old, does not believe it. The contract which locks him in until 2030 has even become a burden according to him. “I can’t imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him in these circumstances. This is problematic.» This statement may be official, but it is not shared by everyone within the club. Since last night and this famous interview which caused a lot of noise, managers, coaches and players have taken a stand, and are not all going in the same direction.

“He is someone who has to endure a lot at his young age. We support it. We believe he has the potential to return to formsays Max Eberl, the sports director, while tempering the situation. It’s legitimate to be worried, especially after what happened.» Before Rummenigge, Uli Hoeness, the honorary president of Bayern, and Jan-Christian Dreesen, the CEO, had expressed their concerns after Musiala’s first discomfort during two friendly matches this summer. According to Bildthere are now two opposing camps on the subject within the club.

On one side we find Hoeness, Rummenigge and the majority of the supervisory board, as well as Dreesen. They would like Musiala to agree to lower his salary since he is no longer as efficient as before. Rummenigge’s statement last night is also seen as a first step of pressure by the clan opposite. This is embodied by the sports management, Max Eberl and Christoph Freund at the head. Vincent Kompany is also their ally in this affair. The technician refused “to enter into this debate» after the match this Friday evening, while affirming that “it is completely normal for people who have done a lot for the club to have their opinion.»

The locker room is obviously on the side of the German international, like Konrad Laimer, also questioned in the mixed zone. “Jamal is a great guy who works incredibly hard every day. Given what I see every day, I am absolutely certain that he will return to his best level. I’m very happy, we’re all very happy to see him back on the pitch, and I’m sure he’ll show everyone what he’s made of.» Musiala made his return to competition yesterday after a muscle problem which kept him away from the field for a month and a half. He played the last 20 minutes against Cologne.

#1454. Romano: Endrick’s agents set for crunch Real Madrid meeting as Milan await news

Endrick’s entourage are expected to meet Real Madrid soon, Fabrizio Romano confirms, with AC Milan awaiting developments.

It seems as though Endrick is Milan’s number one target in view of the winter window. It will take a big fee to prise him away from Real Madrid on a permanent basis, but Gerry Cardinale’s recent words suggest that the Brazilian is the chosen one, and there has been talk of a €70m bid.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Now, it remains to be seen what the margins are for a potential agreement. Los Blancos may seek a buy-back clause, while the will of the head coach Jose Mourinho and of course the player himself must be taken into consideration, given Endrick has spoken of his love for Real.

There is a new update from Fabrizio Romano on his YouTube channel regarding the future of Endrick, and it seems as though a crucial few days are coming up regarding the former Palmeiras starlet.

“This week, some of the most important figures from the agency that represents Endrick, Roc Nation, are expected in Madrid to speak with Endrick and obviously the issue of his situation will have to be addressed,” he said (via MilanNews).

“I have already told you that José Mourinho continues to insist, not only publicly but also privately, to keep him. AC Milan are there, Cardinale has been working on it for some time, and Roma is also interested in Endrick. This operation, for the moment, remains tied to Real Madrid.

“However, the update I am giving you today is precisely this visit by the agents to Endrick. We need to speak with the boy and his family. His father Douglas is also very involved in the decisions, as is Endrick’s wife, it is also a family matter, so we will have to understand the direction to take.

“I repeat that Real Madrid, and especially José Mourinho, intend to keep Endrick until the end of the season, then we will have to see if he will change. something between now and the end of December.

“Milan and Roma should be kept there because their interest is truly concrete and strong, but then everything hinges on Real Madrid. And speaking of visions and strategies, we’ll soon understand if other teams might enter the fray.

“Let me give you an example: in the final days of the summer transfer window, Liverpool, before signing Barcola, had considered adding Endrick to their squad and had even spoken to Endrick’s agents, but Real Madrid wouldn’t hear of it.

“Currently, the Reds are completely complete in attack, so I don’t think they’ll be among the competition for Endrick in January, but we’ll see what kind of situation unfolds.”

#1453. In great shape, Malen’s Roma wants to defeat PSG!

Five goals scored in Parma, a quadruple from Donyell Malen and a fourth consecutive victory in Serie A: AS Roma could not have better prepared for their European meeting against Paris Saint-Germain. Saturday evening, the Giallorossi swept Parma (5-1) at the Ennio-Tardini stadium, confirming their excellent momentum upon returning from the international break. Second in the Italian championship, just two points behind Lazio, Gian Piero Gasperini’s team is establishing itself as one of the most attractive teams at the start of the season. With 36 goals scored in just twelve days, the Romans even displayed a historic offensive performance. You have to go back 76 years to find such a prolific team at this stage of Serie A. Enough to approach the trip to Paris with great confidence, where the reigning double European champions await them.

And this demonstration obviously bears the signature of a man: Donyell Malen. The Dutch international tormented the Parmesan defense with a quadruple, confirming his status as Roma’s main offensive danger. His statistics are dizzying: already 26 goals scored in the calendar year 2026 in the Roman jersey, a performance that no player at the club has achieved since Bobby Manfredini in 1960. An efficiency which also rewards the work of Gasperini, who seems to have found the ideal position to exploit the qualities of the former Borussia Dortmund striker. “Perhaps I played him where he expresses himself best. There are many great strikers in Italy, we can think of Lautaro, but Malen is extraordinary at the moment, especially in the way his characteristics combine with those of our team”greeted the Italian technician after the meeting.

But reducing this Roma to the sole success of Malen would be a mistake. Since the start of the season, Gasperini has built a team capable of stifling its opponents, multiplying dangerous situations and, above all, reacting when put in difficulty. Facing Parma, the Romans had to deal with tougher opposition than the final score suggests. “The result doesn’t really reflect the match. Parma were in good shape, aggressive, and their long balls gave us problems. We conceded a bad goal which could have changed the psychological aspect of the match”recognized the former Atalanta coach. But it was precisely the reaction of his players that impressed him: “We now have the confidence and ability to score and win. This is our greatest quality. We play all our matches with the desire to win them. And we can win them all”. Mental strength that accompanies obvious collective progression, both tactically and physically.

This rise in power comes at the best time for La Louve, who is preparing to meet PSG in the Champions League. And this meeting comes at the best time for the Italian club, in great form, facing a PSG still ambitious, but forced to deal with the absences of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Désiré Doué, two major elements of its offensive sector. The Parisians obviously have the weapons necessary to bring down the Italians, but they will have to be wary of this Roma’s ability to exploit spaces and punish the slightest error. Gasperini can also count on the depth of his squad, an asset that he himself highlighted after the victory in Parma. “That’s the advantage of having a Champions League squad, with five or six quality changes that can turn a match around”. PSG has been warned, this Roma will not come to Paris to make up the numbers.

#1452. Lazio lose Tavares and Sutalo for at least three weeks as Juventus chase 11-point gap

Defenders Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo hurt their hamstrings at Napoli, leaving unbeaten Serie A leaders Lazio short in defence. The setback hits Gattuso's back line just as Juventus return from the break chasing the leaders.

Lazio’s defence has suffered a double blow. Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo were both injured in the 1-1 draw at Napoli. The timing is awkward for the leaders, who resume their league campaign against Lecce on 21 November.

Exact recovery times will only be set once all clinical tests are complete. The early estimate is about 20 days for each player, Sky Sport Italia reported. On that timeline, both miss the home game against Lecce and could return for the trip to Torino on 28 November.

Not every report is that hopeful. Football Italia reported that the pair should miss both the Lecce and Torino games. Under that scenario, they hope to be available again in the first week of December. The match against Atalanta on 6 December is also in doubt.

Tavares has been a real attacking outlet this season. He has one goal and four assists in 11 Serie A games. He also has a long record of muscle injuries. Sutalo has made eight league appearances since joining on loan from Ajax on 22 August.

Lazio must now turn to their alternatives. Alfonso Pedraza, who joined from Villarreal in the summer, is the leading option at left-back. He has played 322 minutes across the league and Coppa Italia. Diogo Leite and Doekhi are competing to replace Sutalo in the middle.

The stand-ins inherit a strong record. Lazio have scored 25 goals and conceded 9 so far. Keeping that defensive record with a reshuffled back line is now Gattuso’s task.

Juventus know Lazio’s quality first-hand. Gattuso’s side won 3-0 in Turin earlier this season. That result still weighs on the table. Five wins, three draws and three defeats make up the Juventus record from their opening games.

— S.S.Lazio (@OfficialSSLazio) November 8, 2026

Two missing defenders will not close the gap on their own. They do, however, give Juventus a window in which the leaders are weaker than usual. Any dropped points by Lazio over the coming rounds would only count if Juventus take care of their own fixtures.

Those fixtures follow Lazio’s closely. Como v Juventus is scheduled for Sunday 29 November at 20:45, the day after Lazio’s game against Torino. Further ahead, Lazio’s aim is to have both defenders fit for the Rome derby on 13 December.

#1451. Real Madrid already has big doubts about its new recruit JJ Gabriel!

It was a soap opera that fascinated England, but not only that. Indeed, the one who is considered the country’s biggest hope, JJ Gabriel, had made the decision to leave Manchester United before signing his first professional contract with the Red Devils. Almost all the big clubs in the Old Continent looked into the matter, and it was ultimately Real Madrid who won the jackpot, ahead of clubs like FC Barcelona or Bayern Munich.

The player’s entourage also had some serious demands, and the amount of the operation is estimated at around 15 million euros. This includes the player’s salary, bonuses, commissions as well as compensation to be paid to Mancunians. Jude Bellingham would even have intervened to convince the attacking midfielder who recently celebrated his 16th birthday, and who should join Real Madrid Castilla, in Spanish D3. If the deal has not yet been made official, the player has already posed with the front page of the newspaper Marca announcing his arrival, which no longer leaves much room for doubt.

But Real Madrid would have already been cooled by certain behaviors of the teenager. A recent video of the player in a Barça store, carrying one of the Catalan club jerseys in his arms, for example circulated on the networks. But above all, as explained The Sunthe Madrid leaders are already very suspicious of the player’s father, who is particularly demanding and already has a rather sulphurous reputation.

In particular, he would have had a very tense relationship with Manchester United, and inevitably, in Madrid, we are already afraid of seeing him reproduce this behavior on the Valdebebas side. They also fear that he could have a bad influence on his son, and are also worried about the father’s actions on social networks. Within the Merengue club, some people, including players, were also surprised to see the young Englishman declare that he dreamed of the Ballon d’Or, without even having played a single professional match. The operation is not a priori in danger, but what is certain is that the behavior of JJ Gabriel and his father will be closely scrutinized in Spain…

#1450. Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”

Tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

“I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”

“It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

“It’s one thing to be nominated, but it’s another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination.”

“The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”

“That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a new level of pressure.”

Tuchel has now claimed that people say the 6-4 against France is “maybe one of their best experiences (watching football) ever”.

Again, not something anyone has said to me. Where is Tuchel finding these people?!

Tuchel on Alexander-Arnold: “He comes as a right back.” Sounds like he agrees with Mourinho that the Real Madrid player is not a midfielder.

Tuchel: “There was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their (the FA’s) mind.”

Tuchel says that 99.9 per cent of fans don’t talk about substitutions. He says they speak about the Mexico game and the Croatia game, their emotions and where they watched the matches.

Sorry, Thomas, that’s not my experience at all. Everyone I speak to says he blew the Argentina game. This sounds a bit deluded. According to Tuchel, I must speak to 0.01 per cent of England fans....

FA technical director John McDermott, who has taken a position at the back of the room to listen, had a little laugh when Tuchel joked that he got told off in his FA review for “my substitutions.”

Tuchel says he felt the “full support from my bosses”.

Warning for Palmer: “It’s one thing to get your ticket back, but it’s another thing to keep it.”

He’s expecting Palmer to step up and show him his Chelsea form.

“When you are a coach, you only win when you win...There’s not much sense torturing ourselves by looking back. I will not allow 30 minutes of the World Cup to determine how we view the World Cup.”

Tuchel says he has no regrets over not taking Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. He says he didn’t have a single sleepless night over his squad selection.

Tuchel says the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”

Tuchel says his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s important to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

He says the downside of having the belief they could go and win it is that it hurts even more that they did not.

Tuchel has said the France third-place game “directs the narrative” of what’s coming for England.

Tuchel will be happy with this so far. Very gentle start from the broadcasters.

No questions from the broadcasters about blowing the lead against Argentina and Tuchel’s opinion about the World Cup. Weird.

Ben White pulled out with an injury after being back to his best. It is unfortunately, a bit of a story for him. Josh King was very close and is on the radar.

“The door is always open through performance, behaviour and commitment.”

“They had a good start to the season. Now it’s a new competition. Some positions have injuries. Palmer has his numbers back and a point to prove. Trent was never non-selectable and comes in as a right back.”

We will be hearing from Tuchel very soon. Lots to discuss but the Palmer and Alexander-Arnold call-ups and his World Cup reflections are at the top of the list.

#1449. GdS: Why Cisse’s position remains a dilemma despite continuous flow of goals

Alphadjo Cisse is one goal away from double figures for the season, and we have not even reached the end of November yet.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, the numbers that Cisse is putting up are those of a centre-forward. He has six goals in 10 Serie A appearances, at an average of one every 74 minutes. In the Europa League he has three (a hat-trick against RB Salzburg), at one every 84 minutes.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yet, his role remains a bit of a mystery. Cisse has his own idea of ​​his preferred position on the pitch, even if he’s a bit vague. Speaking after the match against Frosinone, he hinted that he’d like to move into the attacking midfielder position behind the striker.

“I’d have more fun and entertain the fans. It would also be easier to provide assists for my team-mates, something I enjoy and haven’t yet managed to do at AC Milan,” he confessed to Sky.

In Verona’s youth team, where Cisse first emerged, head coach Paolo Sammarco deployed him as a left-sided attacking midfielder. It was a position in which the then 17-year-old then went on to score 16 league goals in a breakout season.

At Catanzaro, in his first professional stint in Serie B under Alberto Aquilani, the Italian played more or less the same role in a 3-4-2-1 system, sometimes a bit wider. Before the serious injury that caused him to miss the final six months of last season, he has scored six goals in 22 games.

Ruben Amorim initially deployed him as a left-sided winger, also due to Christian Pulisic’s temporary unavailability. He would later move him further forward and more centrally, to take up the spaces a striker would, a position he has played for Italy U21s under Silvio Baldini.

In this position, Cisse can utilise his extraordinary ability to position himself between the ball and the defender, before turning, aiming and often finishing first time. Despite not being physically big (at 180cm tall), he is strong and has a low centre of gravity that makes him tough to bump off the ball.

⚽️ GOAL ALPHADJO CISSE! 🔥 https://t.co/aMIgE9PXHc

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

This is where the dilemma arises. At Verona and Catanzaro, Alphadjo Cisse impressed because of his speed and agility. After the injury and under the watch of Amorim, he has become more of a positioning-based player, barely ever tearing down the flank.

So far this season, he’s attempted only 16 dribbles at just over three per game, and has only succeeded on five. With one successful dribble per game on average, his success rate is just over 31% (FotMob data).

These numbers perhaps help explain Cisse’s progression close to the penalty area, and also a concept that the player himself has repeated in recent months regarding where he is at in his personal development. On Sunday, he declared: “I’m not even halfway to my potential.”

Who knows if Alpha is referring to his overall growth, with horizons still unexplored, or perhaps his post-injury recovery. Amorim will continue to ponder things, but this is far from a headache, because the rule seems to be well established: if Cisse plays, he tends to score.

#1447. Thuram and Locatelli absences leave Juventus midfield thin for four games in 12 days

Khéphren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli will miss the rest of 2026 after knee surgery, leaving Spalletti short in midfield for a congested run of fixtures. Højbjerg has emerged as the name Juventus want to cover the gap in January.

Two senior midfielders will be missing as Juventus head into a congested run of fixtures. Thuram should be back with the group in January, and Locatelli only in the spring, Sport Mediaset reported. Both men are recovering from operations on the right knee.

Thuram underwent chondroplasty to treat patellar chondropathy. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the procedure at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon. Locatelli had his external meniscus sutured, also in Lyon, after spraining the knee against Milan. He was due to start rehabilitation the day after the operation.

Spalletti now has to rely on Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and new signing Pape Matar Sarr in the middle. The run opens with Venezia at 12:30 on 22 November. Omonia visit the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November. The trip to Como follows at 20:45 on 29 November. The sequence closes with a Coppa Italia last-16 tie against Sassuolo.

Como present a sharp test. Fàbregas’s side have 23 points. They play a European fixture on 24 November, five days before they host Juventus.

The table leaves little room for slips. Juventus have 18 points from five wins, three draws and three defeats. They are 11 points behind leaders Lazio and six points off the Champions League places.

Sarr arrived on 1 September on loan from Tottenham until 30 June 2027. Juventus paid a €2.5 million fee plus €0.3 million in additional costs. The deal includes a €27.5 million permanent transfer, spread over three financial years. That becomes compulsory if certain conditions are met during 2026/27. The club describes him as a physically strong box-to-box midfielder. He has more than 100 Premier League appearances and won the 2024/25 Europa League with Spurs.

There is some relief elsewhere in the squad. Nico Gonzalez, Conceição and Cambiaso could all be available for Venezia. Yildiz hopes to return around December.

The absences make a January move for a midfielder more likely. Juventus have three targets for the window: a centre-forward, a defensive midfielder and a left-back. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is the name for midfield, with Sørloth and Miranda also on the list, QS reported.

The profile is clear. Juventus want an experienced midfielder to bridge the gap until Thuram returns and Locatelli follows later. These remain media reports rather than a club statement.

Until then, the existing group must carry the load. The Coppa Italia tie with Sassuolo is set for the Allianz Stadium in Turin on Thursday 3 December at 21:00.

#1446. Roberto De Zerbi defends Mykhailo Mudryk after on-loan star angered Spurs fans with interview gaffes - including admitting he wanted to join Arsenal

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 20 November 2026

Mykhailo Mudryk is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury.

Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years.

He also risked the wrath of Spurs fans by admitting he only made the move across London to recover his fitness before returning to Stamford Bridge where Blues boss Xabi Alonso was 'counting on him'.

And he managed to annoy both Chelsea and Spurs fans by revealing, during the same YouTube interview, that he wanted to sign for Arsenal when he moved to the Premier League in January 2023 but his agent forced through the move with the best commission.

'I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy,' said Spurs boss De Zerbi, who worked with the Ukraine international at Shakhtar Dontetsk and convinced him to resist interest from Brentford and Coventry and be reunited in North London.

'He's a good player. He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he's playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a big club, like the other clubs, not less at all.'

Mykhailo Mudryk admitted he joined Tottenham to regain fitness before returning to Chelsea, while also stating he had wanted to sign for Arsenal in 2023 before his transfer to the Blues

Roberto De Zerbi acknowledged Tottenham fans' views on Mudryk's comments, but insisted the winger has 'suffered a lot' following his doping ban

Chelsea paid £86million for Mudryk but he made little impression before he was hit with a four-year ban in 2024, which was wiped out this summer enabling him to return to competition.

'He has no responsibility in this part,' said De Zerbi. 'Now his focus is just on the ball or just on the football. He has a big chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club. He knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play.

'He knows I give him total confidence to show what he is. So to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction. But I think he's working hard to recover and to play earlier.'

Mudryk made his Spurs debut as a sub at Nottingham Forest in September but injured an ankle in training a few days later. He was initially expected to be out for two months with Saturday's game against Ipswich his target to return.

'The plan was to be available for Ipswich or Sunderland,' said De Zerbi, who will serve a touchline ban against Ipswich for three yellow cards. 'Then he felt not pain but he was not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we're going to see the situation.'

James Maddison's limited involvement for Tottenham relates to a niggling hip injury dating back to pre-season.

Maddison has been an unused sub in two Spurs games since limping off when the problem flared up at Chelsea, on his second start of the season and his second start in six days.

Roberto De Zerbi confirmed ahead of Saturday's game against Ipswich that it had been the same problem which dogged Maddison through the summer as he fought back from a serious knee injury.

The Spurs boss revealed how his physical condition had suffered from not training regularly and reminded the 29-year-old England midfielder he could only make an impact in the Premier League in peak condition.

De Zerbi confirmed James Maddison is available to face Ipswich but stressed the midfielder needs to push himself to reach his peak physical condition

'It is not a big injury, but he was not able to work,' explained De Zerbi. 'He had a problem with his hip. The same as preseason. It's not a big problem but if you don't work consistently you lose the physical condition and to play in this level of competition you have to stay in the top physical condition.'

Maddison, who turns 30 on Monday, missed most of last season with a cruciate knee injury and has played only 195 minutes this season. His return was further complicated by a shoulder injury after coming on at Brentford on the opening game of the season.

'He is still young, 29 years is not old,' said De Zerbi. 'He has to push and demand of himself the top in terms of physical condition, because if he is 80 or 90 per cent of his physical condition he makes the difference for us, he changes the games.'

Maddison and Destiny Udogie have both trained fully through the international break and are available to face Ipswich.

'He worked very well from the Wednesday after Leeds,' said De Zerbi. 'From Chelsea to the Leeds game, he worked just three times on the pitch at the training ground.

'If you don't work during the week you risk injury and lose the normal physical condition you need to play Premier League. The same for Udogie. When they work and are fit to work, they have many chances to play, especially Maddison because a special player.'

Maddison's first start of the season came against Coventry when he scored the opener and inspired Spurs to their first win. He barely trained but started again in the win at Chelsea five days later, where he broke down early in the second half and was replaced by Conor Gallagher.

De Zerbi made it clear there were no problems connected to Maddison being pictured out at a pub in Coventry after the defeat at Leeds. It was the last game before the international break and the first of three days off.

'I am angry because next time he has to invite me,' joked the Spurs boss and he added: 'I am happy. I know when my players work well. If they are serious on the pitch, off the pitch they can do what they want. I'm not a policeman.

'James is top professional, top guy, top player. The private life is not our problem if they work well and they are serious, and give their best for the club, the shirt and the fans, and he is perfect when it comes to that.'

#1445. Juventus and Torino the only Serie A sides without a penalty either way after 11 rounds

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the new refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

The trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

The contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

The run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

The first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

#1443. Watch: Amorim’s passionate ‘biggest mistake’ response which achieved viral status

Ruben Amorim’s response to a question regarding AC Milan’s squad building has gone viral on social media.

Given his past at Sporting CP, who are one of the three biggest clubs in Portugal, and Manchester United, arguably the biggest club in England, Amorim is no stranger to having his words in interviews and press conferences picked apart.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, we wrote at length about what his comments told us both before and after the derby win against Inter and the defeat to Ferencvaros. The Portuguese speaks his mind and leaves little to the imagination, doing so with clarity and often with charisma too.

A clip of one of the responses he gave in his pre-Frosinone presser has been doing the rounds on social media, gathering over two million views. When asked about the idea of spending money in January, Amorim’s reply was a typically impassioned one.

“That is the biggest mistakes of the big clubs: thinking that [we] look at the table. If we are near, let’s invest, crazy invest. If we are not near, let’s not invest. I think the key point is [to] have a long-term plan,” he said.

“If you lose all the games, sack the manager – that is normal (smiles). I’m not talking about that. But what I’m saying is that: stick with your plan. We have a plan. What kind of player we want. [One who] is able to make all the runs that we want. He has the character that we want.

“Not a big star – like a guy that is composed and come here to be one of the part of the team. If we have that really clear and we go for the best that we can. Young, old – it’s better young in this moment. But if you have a clear plan, don’t look at the table.

“Look at the table to evaluate the process, but to buy, to spend money for the five next years, don’t look at the table. And I think that is the biggest mistake of the clubs: like putting all the [effort into] trying to be champion by spending money. That is the biggest mistake.

“So we have a clear plan. It doesn’t matter the table. We are going to address what we want in a very clear way. So that is not going to change. And I look at the table. I look at our players… we can do better.

“Can we win against Ferencvaros, a very good team? Can we play better against that team? We can, with our players. So we have a clear process. So we are not going to change what we want because we look at the table in December or in January. So we have a clear plan what to do.”

#1442. Celtic boss O'Neill seeks Europa League stand-in as Baur set for lengthy spell on the sidelines

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026

Martin O'Neill will weigh up replacing Mika Baur in the Europa League squad after the midfielder was ruled out for up to 10 weeks with an ankle injury.

The German hobbled off late on in Celtic's win over Kilmarnock almost a fortnight ago with a scan subsequently revealing that he sustained ligament damage.

One of the Parkhead side's star men since signing from Paderborn in the summer, Baur's absence is a major blow for O'Neill ahead of a defining period in the season.

While the manager will look to the likes of Oliver Sorensen and Joel van den Berg to step up domestically, he will also consider using a UEFA rule to make a change to his European squad ahead of Thursday's match away to Torreense in Portugal.

The rule allows clubs to make an alteration to the squad they submitted for the group stage if the injury is expected to sideline the player for more than 60 days from when it occurred.

Van den Berg, Jota, Landon Emenalo and Shim Mheuka weren't on the original 25-man list so would be options to be drafted in.

German midfielder Mika Baur could miss up to 10 weeks of action after injuring his ankle

'I would definitely check with the medical staff and Mika, for a start,' said O'Neill.

'And speaking to him yesterday, he's really upbeat about it. Obviously, he will have that boot on for a few weeks.

'I suppose deep down, if it was, let's say, 10 weeks, that's taking you right through to the end of January. I can't see us seeing him in the next six weeks.'

Baur's form following his £4.5million move has been good enough for him to win his first full cap for Germany after being called up by new manager Jurgen Klopp.

'He was doing great for us,' added O'Neill. 'It is a blow. And it seemed so innocuous at the time.

'I thought that he'd been kicked, but it was the other foot he'd landed on. It's just gone over. It's a real shame. He was playing great for us.

'There's things that he can't do for a while.'

O'Neill revealed that Benjamin Nygren is also an injury doubt for Saturday's match with St Mirren.

'He didn't train today, but we'll see how he is in the morning,' he explained. 'He's got a sore heel. He missed out the second game in Sweden's run.

'He's been feeling it for a couple of weeks, so we'll see how he is tomorrow.'

19-year-old summer signing Joel van den Berg could make his first Celtic outing this weekend

Van den Berg hasn't played for the first team since joining from PSV Eindhoven for £3.4m in the summer with an injury impeding his progress.

But the 19-year-old could be in line for his first-team debut against the Buddies.

'I had a little chat to him,' said O'Neill. 'He trained this morning, he didn't train yesterday. We played a bounce game during the week, Tuesday against St Johnstone.

'He played in that game, came off and he was definitely limping for a while. He had a couple of days' treatment.

'In the overall scheme of things, whether it's tomorrow or in the next week or two, I'd hope to see him make his mark.

'As I said to him yesterday, "When you get in, it's really up to you".'

O'Neill anticipates a stern test from a St Mirren side who often have not picked up the positive results their performances have merited under Craig McLeish.

'The overall job he's done has been terrific, really terrific,' said the Celtic manager.

'They're having a wee tough time at this minute, obviously, with results, but his overall contributions, I'd say it's been excellent.

'There are some really fine coaches in Scotland, genuinely, and I don't want to sound patronising or sycophantic, but there are.

'We were up against one two weeks ago against Kilmarnock [Neil McCann], so I've got a lot of time for those boys who are coming through and who, to my mind, are every bit as good of coaches as quite a number down south.'

#1441. Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it quickly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

Both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another new signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “big lesson” for his players.

“There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta said. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

“It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

“It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta said. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, said. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”

Two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

When you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a big lesson for us to learn. If I have to describe how the team has played and competed in the last six or seven weeks, has been expectational but today has been a big lesson.

A very disappointing result and performance. Full credit to Brighton the manner they went about the game, they were a different gear from us. We didn’t do the basics right for long periods, especially in the first half. We didn’t win enough duels, and any second balls and that stretches you.

We were poor technically when we had the ball in our own half, we didn’t apply the principles that you need against a team that wants to press you man to man.

Arteta: "There are certain basics that you need to accomplish in the Premier League that we were very far from. The amount of technical errors we did... we didn't respect any principle of play. We were always on the back foot. They had another edge."

Beating the current champions and maybe the best team in England is something special. The result is nice but the performance is what makes it special, the boys showed real courage, real intensity and they were horrible to play against because we did the basics right.

Intensity, intensity, winning the personal duels...we have to have the belief to compete with the best teams in the league. My players really trust each other on the pitch. If one player is out then another can replace him.

Overall we wanted to be really good in every phase. We needed to be at the highest level. We go game by game. After the international break we have a lot of games. After wins like this we have to stay humble and understand why we had this win. We have to keep on going.

Our 125 anniversary & one of the best days! 💫 pic.twitter.com/YbZLTFPpWN

I thought we showed great intensity, waited for mistakes and punished Arsenal. It was a strong performance, a very complete performance.

We won the ball high up and attacked really fast. After the last two wins we are full of confidence and wanted to finish really strong before the international break.

I feel really good. I can’t complain. I just try to help the team when I can. I really enjoy life in Brighton, I’m loving it.

I know after the international break we play every three days and a lot of the lads are not used to that. It will be tough. I hope we can compete. We have a big squad this season.

Pascal Gross pulling the strings. 🔎 @Microsoft pic.twitter.com/DAgVsG2B3W

Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions in three consecutive seasons.

Like Everton, Newcastle labour to a home win which should have been more comfortable. It would have been had Wissa scored his penalty, but it was a nervy finish as Hull pushed for an equaliser after Cho’s goal.

Everton up to fifth but they made hard work of that against Ipswich’s 10 men, but Thierno Barry’s goal proves the difference. Barry unfortunate that his second did not stand because of a contentious offside check.

One of the outstanding team performances of the season so far from Brighton, and it will take some beating between now and May. Arsenal were loose defensively in open play and from set-pieces, and were smothered by Brighton’s pressing. Arteta’s team beaten for the first time this season and emphatically so. Arsenal’s first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023.

Just three minutes of stoppage time remaining, but Hull are still pushing bodies forward.

Hull are knocking on the door at St James’ Park, and Newcastle are hanging on to their lead rather than pressing for a third goal.

Matt O’Riley has missed two great chances to make it four. Brighton have not given Arsenal a sniff. It will be interesting to hear how stern Arteta is in his post-match assessment.

Kai Havertz shoots straight at the goalkeeper when clean through, and that is surely Arsenal’s last chance of an unlikely comeback gone. Brighton have pushed Arsenal back for much of the season half, they have not been sitting on a lead.

At St James’ Park, Hull have pulled a goal back through Cho to set up a nervy finish for Newcastle.

The forward is shown a second yellow card for diving, and Ipswich’s hopes appear to be dwindling at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

What a farcical five minutes we have had, from an absurd disallowed goal for Everton to a ridiculous red card for Abdul Fatawu, banished for a second bookable offence - which was diving. There is going to be plenty said about Thierno Barry’s second goal being chalked out because, when you see it, you will wonder what it was for. These are the situations with which I struggle most - if players do not appeal for a wrongdoing, if they don’t feel they have been the victims of an injustice, why are officials getting involved?

Thierno Barry thought he had made it two for Everton, but the goal has been ruled out because Brennan Johnson was judged to be interfering with play and offside. You’re never getting those this weekend after the Enzo Fernandez incident.

Arsenal undone from a corner, swung to the back post and Chema Andres rose above everyone to head home.

This is a remarkable performance by Brighton, who have battered and bullied the champions from the start. Three-nil, and they have even beaten Arsenal at their own game by scoring a set-piece.

I am struggling to remember the last time Arsenal were overrun and outplayed as comprehensively as this. It’s a thrashing.

No half-time subs from Mikel Arteta, which is a little surprising given Arsenal’s predicament.

The undisputed highlight of the afternoon so far – Raspberry Beret has just been played during the half-time interval and you will agree that this is Prince’s finest work. We feel the need to bring this to your attention because, really, the final 15 minutes of the first half were a hotchpotch and if Everton don’t raise themselves, they will find trouble.

Just before half-time at St James’ Park, Konstantinos Tzolakis saved Yoane Wissa’s penalty.

Another shot from outside the box as Arsenal’s defenders backed off, and the Greek striker found the bottom corner. What a first half for Brighton, Arsenal need to pull something out of the fire in the second half. Just before the goal, Saka had a chance after a deflected Odegaard shot.

Brighton’s second goal was an even better hit than their first. End-to-end football resulted in Kostoulas having space 20 yards from Arsenal’s goal. It’s another thumping low finish. Brilliant, breathless half of football by Brighton.

As half-time approaches, Arsenal have mustered just one shot on goal worth 0.03 expected goals. When they have moved the ball beyond Brighton’s press, they have not done anywhere near enough with it.

This fixture last season was especially bad-tempered, with the Brighton fans (and manager) repeatedly accusing Arsenal of time-wasting. The memories of that defeat are clearly still fresh in the minds of the Brighton supporters, who are roaring with rage at every perceived delay by the visitors, despite the fact that Arsenal are losing. The bad blood is adding to the intensity of the occasion.

Ipswich don’t play like a team that is short of confidence and quality. You might assume, if you haven’t seen much of them, that they are destined for a season of toil but there is definite quality with Gary O’Neill’s ranks, including Abdul Fatawu, who has been magnetic in drawing your eye to him. They might be a goal down but they are playing as if they are a goal in front.

Arsenal had just enjoyed a spell of control, but trail to a goal from one of the league’s in-form players. Gross whips a shot from just outside the box around Raya and in off the post.

Brighton have the lead at the Amex and it’s their captain, Pascal Gross, who has provided it. Superb long-range effort, in off the near post. On the overall balance of play, Brighton deserve that. It’s reward for their courage and willingness to go after Arsenal, rather than sitting back.

It took almost 20 minutes but Arsenal have found their feet in this game now. They are starting to find avenues through Brighton’s aggressive pressing and have made a few promising runs in behind, through Havertz and Saka. This is a high quality match.

No goals at the Amex, but Brighton are the team making the running, Arsenal struggling to play out from their own half and are yet to register a shot on goal.

Barry kept himself onside and turned the ball into the back of the net with his stomach. He did well to avoid a handball.

Bright start from Everton and they have the goal they deserve, albeit it came in fortuitous circumstances. James Tarkowski’s volley clattered into Thierno Barry and the deflection took it away from Christian Walton in Ipswich’s goal. Barry now has five goals for the season and, while he is raw, it’s an invaluable contribution.

A storming response to a bad night at Leeds from Newcastle, and it looks like being a long afternoon for Hull. Two down in seven minutes.

What a start for Newcastle United and what will really please manager Matthias Jaissle is the way both goals have come from his players winning important tackles.

The German was incensed by the lack of physicality and intensity in the heavy defeat to Leeds on Monday but the first goal for Joe Wilock came when Lewis Miley won a tackle on the edge of the Hull penalty box.

The second came when Sven Botman came away with the ball just inside his own half. On both occasions Harvey Barnes provided the assist. A short, intricate pass to Willock inside the box and then a surging, twisting run from the halfway line and the perfectly timed pass to Lewis Hall who stroked a first time shot into the bottom corner.

Hull have been outfought so far which is precisely the response Newcastle’s manager had demanded.

The home team are pressing high and all over Arsenal in the early stages. Raya has just made a save to deny Kostoulas.

Brighton have started brilliantly against the champions. They are hunting like wolves, pressing Arsenal with remarkable intensity. We have played seven minutes and I don’t think the ball has left Arsenal’s half.

Big chance for Everton to take the lead, but after great skill to turn his man at the edge of the box Brennan Johnson shoots wide with only the goalkeeper to beat.

The perfect start for Newcastle with all their injuries: Joe Willock has put the home side in a strong position against Hull with a clean strike inside three minutes.

We are under way at the Amex, St James’ Park and the Hill Dickinson.

Another famous face in the stands at Hill Dickinson Stadium today but this time it’s not about politicians. Wayne Rooney is here to watch his boyhood club and he will be hoping Everton can go into the international break unbeaten. An extra special cheer too before kick-off for Jarrad Branthwaite, who has just been called up for England duty. Plenty of Premier League clubs would like to sign Branthwaite, if they were given half a chance, but David Moyes has made it quite clear that Branthwaite: “Isn’t for sale - I want to keep my best players.”

He was not part of the match-day squad at Sunderland but Ben White’s injury has opened up a place, and Dowman fully deserves it after his two goals against Ipswich in the League Cup. Sam Dean has the story of his rise to stardom as well as what Arsenal are doing to nurture such a special talent.

Brighton are wearing a special “125 anniversary” kit today, to mark 125 years since the club was formed in 1901. It’s inspired by the colours of their first ever kit, which means an all-blue shirt, pale gold shorts and dark socks. Personally I would not allow such nonsense. But I don’t make the rules.

Spurs scored two late goals to salvage some pride against Aston Villa, but it is another defeat for Roberto De Zerbi’s team who have two points from five games. This Emi Buendia screamer put the game out of reach.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd

It has been a term tossed around liberally at Newcastle United since Matthias Jaissle arrived as manager, but what does “vertical football” actually mean?

It is the new buzzword in football analysis, the latest fashionable phrase to describe a “new” style of football, and it has been referenced multiple times by both Jaissle and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, since the German coach’s appointment last month.

For some of us of a certain age, vertical football just seems like clever new terminology to describe an old idea.

We are getting to the stage where we really need to start asking questions about Tino Livramento’s injury record.

The right back was due to start for Newcastle against Hull City this afternoon – his first start since April – but has picked up another injury.

That will surely mean he is out of the England squad for the Nations League having also picked up a tournament-ending injury at the World Cup in the summer before the first group game.

Livramento only played 17 Premier League games for Newcastle last season, scuppering his chances of a summer move to Arsenal, missing huge chunks of the season with groin and hamstring issues.

Injuries are already cutting deep into the Newcastle squad, with four teenagers on the bench for the visit of Hull. None have played in the first team before and three of them – Michael Mills, Mason Miley and Kyrian Thompson are just 17–years-old.

Newcastle wanted a younger team this season but not this young. It was interesting to hear Matthias Jaissle talk before the game. He knows how tough this season could be with so little experience in the side.

Lewis Dunk is a surprise absentee for Brighton, it can only be because of injury, and Hurzeler has preferred Diego Gomez to the lively Yalcouye who was very threatening at Old Trafford and Coventry. He could be a handful off the bench.

Good news for Arsenal: Jurrien Timber is finally fit enough to start a match again. This is his first start since mid-March and his return is timely, given the absence of Ben White through injury. It’s also a first Premier League start for Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes, who comes into the midfield after his impressive performance off the bench at Sunderland last weekend.

Very excited for this one today. Arsenal have won all seven of their matches so far. Only once before in their history have they won their first eight games of a season - that was in 1903, when they were playing in the Second Division as Woolwich Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/iNBxoHl4Gc

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

#1440. How to use home and away stats before betting

Six home wins from ten matches describe past results, not a 60% forecast for the next fixture. Before setting that record beside 1xbet football betting odds, check the strength of the opponents behind it. Compare the hosts’ home performances with the visitors’ away performances, then establish what those records suggest about your chosen market.

Start by identifying the market you want to assess. A home-win bet and a bet on the home team to score two or more goals have different requirements. For a home-win bet, the hosts must win the match. For a home team over 1.5 goals bet, the hosts must score at least two goals, regardless of the final result.

Use the same competition and season for both teams, while for the statistical source make sure to use the appropriate venue filter of your choice. Record:

For a team-goals bet, count how often the required total was reached. A team scoring six once and then recording five blanks has the same average as another scoring once in all six games. Only the first reached the two-goal threshold. Repeat the count for the visitors conceding at least two.

Keep the overall season record alongside the split. Three home fixtures give you little evidence of a lasting venue-specific pattern.

Suppose the two teams have these hypothetical records:

You need to divide total goals by appearances. Then, analyze those figures in light of the averages of the league in terms of scoring at home and away. The home side scores 1.8 goals at home and the away side concedes 1.7 when playing away from home. Therefore, you should be interested in analyzing the scoring situation for the home side. However, it does not mean that because you’ve averaged these numbers, the home side is going to score 1.75 goals.

Now compare goals with expected goals (xG). The hosts’ attacking xG averages 1.55 per match, below their actual scoring rate. Inspect the chances behind the difference before assuming the higher rate will continue. The visitors’ away expected goals against average 1.50. Compare that with the hosts’ attacking xG, then examine shot maps or match reports for the chances involved.

Expected goals estimates shot quality, using the likelihood of similar chances becoming goals. Use one provider consistently because models differ.

View all relevant results. Identify home victories over weaker sides and also away defeats against stronger opponents. Compare today’s opponents to these as well.

Also check out all instances where margins are inordinate. If one home result produced six out of the eighteen goals, it makes one third of the whole total. Assess all other results to find out whether the method of play remains consistent.

Consider all red cards and penalties. Keep those results, but mind that some results occurred under unusual situations. Don’t delete unwelcome results from your records to make the average better.

If several options are produced by using the filters, then compare their total odds with the sum of money already set aside.

Before relying on the split, compare the likely lineup with the players responsible for it. An absent starting striker matters differently from a reserve missing the matchday bench.

Check whether a coaching change falls within the sample. If it does, inspect results before and after the appointment rather than treating them as one unchanged team.

Confirm the venue too. A nominal home team playing at a neutral ground does not provide the usual setting represented by its home record.

Look at the selection once more, keeping the current odds in mind. Calculate the implied probability of decimal odds by dividing 100 by the odds. In the case of odds of 1.80, you get something like 55.6% in terms of probability.

Of course, the fact that hosts won six out of ten home games is not enough for such an estimation. You should utilize the split in your broader analysis of the meeting and not take the average of hosts’ winning percentage and guests’ losing percentage to calculate the probability.

If you cannot find support for your probability estimation, then do not place the bet at this stage. Make a note of the uncertainty, as sometimes the substitute striker can be unconfirmed or the evidence in favor of the hosts is insignificant given the strength of their opponents.

#1439. Zhegrova plays 82 minutes in Kosovo’s 0-0 with Israel before Dublin decider for second

With Edon Zhegrova in the starting line-up, ten-man Kosovo held Israel to a goalless draw, a result that leaves them second in Nations League Group B3. The run-out gives a Juventus forward who rarely starts for his club valuable match fitness while Pierre Kalulu is injured.

In Pristina, the Juventus forward Edon Zhegrova was Kosovo’s main attacker against Israel.

Zhegrova tested Israel’s defence a couple of times in the first half but faded after the break, according to TuttoJuve. Dion Kacuri came on in his place.

Below Kosovo, Ireland have 5 points and Israel 3. Austria beat the Republic of Ireland 1-0 on the same Saturday.

Kosovo’s campaign has been uneven. They opened by beating the Republic of Ireland 1-0 on 24 September. Three days later they lost 3-1 away to Austria on 27 September. On matchday 3, they had also drawn 0-0 with Israel.

The final round pairs the Republic of Ireland with Kosovo and Israel with Austria. That leaves Ireland, sitting just below Kosovo, hosting the side directly above them. Zhegrova is set to be central to Kosovo’s hopes of holding on to second place.

For Juventus, the significance lies in the minutes. Zhegrova has started only once since joining the club. He sits low in Spalletti’s pecking order and has mostly featured in short spells off the bench.

More than 80 minutes as Kosovo’s focal point gives him match fitness. That could prove useful before Juventus face Venezia in Serie A and Omonia in the Europa League.

The squad is stretched. Scans at J|medical on 9 November found a low-grade injury to Pierre Kalulu’s left biceps femoris. The defender had felt muscle discomfort in his left thigh after the draw at Fiorentina. France withdrew him from their squad. The midfield is also short of bodies.

Spalletti has made clear he sees potential in the winger. “Edon se si completa un po’ può diventare un crack,” the coach said. If Edon rounds out his game a little, he can become a star.

We draw 0–0 with Kosovo in the UEFA Nations League. pic.twitter.com/SSS4UTPpw4

— ISRAEL FA (@ISRAELFA) November 14, 2026

Other clubs are paying attention too. Near the end of the summer window, Al-Ittihad made a move for the winger, and Monaco are also interested, Eurosport Italia reported. A strong finish to the international window would do his standing no harm, in Turin or elsewhere.

First comes Dublin. Kick-off at the Aviva Stadium is at 7.45pm UK time, with second place in the group at stake.
