#1438. CM: Gimenez could terminate Porto loan early and return to Milan – the situation

Santiago Gimenez left AC Milan in the summer, but he may be returning before the end of his loan deal next summer.

It’s fair to say that Gimenez is one of the most difficult signings to assess from Milan in recent years. On paper, it made plenty of sense why he was right to arrive; he was firing in the Champions League, he had no difficulty scoring in the league and there was the added bonus of him being young and a fan of the club.

With goals against elite teams in Europe too, it made sense why he’d be able to have a successful career at San Siro. Performing on the biggest stage seemingly wasn’t an issue.

So, when he started brightly, fans thought the Rossoneri had struck gold. Yet, that form quickly came undone and Gimenez began to show glimpses, rather than actually developing a portfolio of goalscoring.

After almost being forced out of the club last summer, an injury-ridden campaign effectively ended his time with the Diavolo and he was loaned out in the summer. Yet, he could already be heading back to Italy.

As Calciomercato.com writes, it’s highly unlikely that Porto will activate the €18m buy clause in his deal, and it’s even possible that he doesn’t see out the complete spell of his loan. He’s the third-choice striker, with only four appearances in the Portuguese top flight and one penalty goal; it’s hardly form that warrants making his stay permanent.

Now, ahead of the January mercato, a meeting is planned with Rafaela Pimenta to discuss what would be best for his career. A return to Milanello cannot be ruled out, but it wouldn’t be permanent. He’s not part of Ruben Amorim’s plans, so a new destination would need to be found.

What is for sure, though, is that his value has only dropped further with his Portuguese adventure…

#1437. Çelik pulled from Türkiye XI with left hamstring tightness as Kalulu is already out

Zeki Çelik was withdrawn from Türkiye's starting line-up in Bordeaux after feeling tightness in the same left thigh muscle he injured in October. With Pierre Kalulu already sidelined, Juventus face tests that could leave them without both main right-sided defenders for Venezia and Omonia.

Zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux. The Juventus full-back was named in Türkiye’s starting line-up for Sunday’s Nations League match against France. His left hamstring tightened up as he went through the warm-up. He was taken out of the matchday squad as a precaution. Barış Alper Yılmaz started in his place.

An Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead. Abdülkerim Bardakcı scored a late reply for Türkiye. The result left France top of Nations League Group A1 with 13 points. They are through to the quarter-finals, which are due next March.

Çelik now returns to Turin for tests at J|Medical. Those results will decide how Juventus line up at the back after the international break.

The location is what worries Juventus. Çelik was substituted at half-time in the 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes. His scans took place on the morning of Friday 23 October. He began a rehabilitation programme straight away and was expected back after the November break.

Tuttosport counted him among Spalletti’s first returning players, alongside Vicario and Gatti. The paper placed the Bordeaux problem in the biceps femoris of his left thigh. That is the same area as the October injury.

Çelik had only just returned after weeks out. That is why the warm-up incident has raised fears of a relapse. No diagnosis has yet been confirmed.

Juventus were already without Pierre Kalulu. He picked up the injury in the game against Fiorentina. He began treatment and was withdrawn from the France squad. Sky Sport Italia expected him to be out for about three weeks. That would rule him out of both the Venezia and Omonia matches.

If Çelik’s problem proves to be a relapse, Spalletti could be without both of his main right-sided defenders for those two games. The schedule offers little room for recovery. The Omonia match is the second of four games in 12 days.

The league position adds pressure. After 11 rounds Juventus are seventh in Serie A with 18 points. Their record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats.

Venezia visit Turin first, at 12:30 on 22 November in round 12 of Serie A. Omonia then come to the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November in the Europa League league phase.

#1435. McKennie says USA players could follow Pochettino to Manchester United

Weston McKennie has said USA players could follow Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United, days after his national team coach took the job there. Juventus, already without Thuram and Locatelli, now face pressure to rule out a mid-season sale.

The question put to Weston McKennie was whether USA players might follow their coach to Old Trafford. His answer was that it could potentially happen.

McKennie called the speculation inevitable. He said many USA players are due to change clubs within the next year, calciomercato.com reported.

Pochettino was asked about the same subject. He said now was not the right time to discuss it. He added that United are among the very top clubs and a dream for many players.

Pochettino and his staff remain in charge of the USA for two games against Haiti, on 14 and 17 November. United agreed with the federation that the staff would be released once those national-team duties were over. Pochettino became USA head coach in September 2024. His record with the national team stands at 21 wins, 12 defeats and two draws from 35 matches.

The comments land awkwardly in Turin. Reports had already linked United with a January move for the American. Juventus regard him as central to Luciano Spalletti’s plans and are reluctant to let him leave mid-season, ESPN reported.

His contract, which runs until June 2030, offers the club some protection. It was signed only months before Pochettino’s switch to English football.

McKennie arrived from Schalke 04 in August 2020. His value to Spalletti lies in his flexibility.

The club noted in its renewal announcement that he had been used on both flanks under Spalletti. He had also recently played as a striker.

The timing makes McKennie harder to replace. He is one of the few senior midfielders Spalletti still has available.

Thuram is out until 2027 after knee surgery. Captain Manuel Locatelli also faces a long absence after twisting his right knee against Milan. He had surgery in Lyon on 8 September to repair the external meniscus, and Corriere dello Sport put his lay-off at five to six months.

Losing him in January would thin the squad further at a delicate point of the season. Juventus are chasing a Champions League place. Qualification is key to the club’s finances.

That is why the club’s stance matters as much as the player’s words.

McKennie’s own answer was measured. He said nobody knows which players a coach really wants.

For now, the pressure falls on Juventus. A clear statement ruling out a January sale would end the debate. Silence would leave it open until the window.

The next step comes at Old Trafford. Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United from 18 November, and his first squad decisions will show whether the interest is real.

#1434. Can Celtic boss Martin O'Neill muddle through until January cavalry arrives?

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026

Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.

Since the first act of this season, a narrow win over Dundee, Martin O’Neill’s side have occupied a place of uncertainty.

Those who have taken the occasional stellar display to be indicative of a corner being turned have been left feeling like fools.

There remain too many shortcomings in the squad, too many question marks hovering above too many players to ever feel that it has left inconsistency behind. The fan base has good reason not to quite trust it.

How could it be otherwise when the clean sheet claimed against bottom side Killie was the first in seven matches?

Kasper Hogh, the club’s record signing at £11million, hasn’t scored in his last 16 outings in green and white.

Martin O'Neill admits it has taken longer than he'd have liked for the new recruits to settle

O’Neill’s options on the flanks include one player in Jota, who’s getting back from a long-term injury, and another in Yang Hyun-jun, who was recently sidelined for six weeks.

There’s a veteran in James Forrest, Seb Tounekti, not exactly the bravest of souls, and Haissem Hassan, a £6m signing who evidently believes defensive work is optional.

It says much that Callum Osmand, a centre-forward now trying to cut it on the flank, has become a fans’ favourite after just 13 senior appearances.

The concerns of the manager now extend to the middle of the park where Mika Baur may be out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

With Benjamin Nygren also a doubt to face St Mirren, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and/or Joel van den Berg could be teamed up with skipper Callum McGregor.

We’re assuredly about to discover if this squad has more about it than the results and performances to this stage have suggested.

‘We can make big improvements, there’s no question about it,’ said the manager.

‘Top of the league, it is nice to be in that position. But other than a number of matches where I think we’ve played very, very well... maybe the Besiktas game, maybe the Hearts game, it’s been really hard work for us.

‘That’s maybe a combination of things. Young and slightly more experienced players coming into the football club, getting to know the club, getting to know the players.

‘That’s taken a bit of time. I didn’t expect it to work immediately overnight.

German midfielder Mika Baur is set to miss around 10 weeks with an ankle ligament injury

‘But they’re at a club where settling in is something they’ve got to do pretty quickly.’

Starting with the visit of the Paisley men, Celtic have 10 games up to and including the trip to Ibrox on January 3.

That encompasses two assignments on the road in the Europa League — Torreense and Omonia Nicosia.

O’Neill’s men also visit Tynecastle, Dens Park, Pittodrie and Tannadice in the league.

As they prepare to put up the Christmas decorations on the Celtic Way, O’Neill could privately be forgiven for wishing the festive season away.

January 5 is the day on which the transfer window in Scotland opens and you can’t help but wonder what Celtic’s prospects for the season will look like at that point.

While Camilo Duran and Baur have contributed, the bulk of the business done in the summer again looks to have been sub-standard.

To stand a chance of retaining the title, O’Neill badly needs several big-hitters to come in without delay in the New Year.

‘We’re absolutely looking at players now,’ he stressed. ‘I suppose every single club is doing that. And the quicker you can get somebody in, the better.

‘We’ve seen when people are fit, we will have numbers. We just need a bit of quality.’

Camilo Duran has been one of very few summer arrivals to have made an impact at Celtic

Until such time as he can call for the cavalry, O’Neill has no choice but to make do and mend.

On the chances of prioritising the league and playing a weakened side in Europe, the veteran is clear.

‘Domestic football is really important to the football club, of course,’ he said. ‘But you’d still want to try and make some show in Europe. And we’ve found that difficult.

‘I genuinely thought against Besiktas we did really fine in the game, we didn’t over-press because they could play through you.

‘There are certain moments even in domestic football when teams can play through you. Kilmarnock caused us plenty of problems.

‘I just think we’ve got to improve in the domestic games. We’ve got to be more aggressive in the sense of taking games to people and being less passive in periods of games.’

O’Neill clearly needs more — much more — from so many individuals if he’s to get through the shark-infested waters of the next six weeks unscathed.

Hassan didn’t even make the matchday squad for Kilmarnock, a move which was interpreted by many as being a boot up the backside by a boss who’s been underwhelmed by his work without the ball.

‘We left out a number of players,’ O’Neill stressed. ‘I wouldn’t read as much into that, because a few will come back.

‘My job is not to please everyone, otherwise we’d have 26 players playing at one time.

O'Neill has backed misfiring striker Kasper Hogh to end his barren streak in front of goal

‘I did a thing with corporate fans the other night, we had a bit of fun with some questions.

‘Apparently something came out that he [Hassan] was the most unpopular player in the dressing room, which is not true.

‘I didn’t say this. I was joking about my own unpopularity, as a player, because all I did was moan.

‘I did say about unpopularity, there’s at least one more unpopular. The crowd wanted to know but I didn’t tell them! I left it hanging. But it was tongue-in-cheek, apart from the part about me being unpopular, which I was.’

The form of Hogh is no laughing matter. The Dane looked the part when he claimed a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9, but that is beginning to feel like ancient history.

For his effort against the Ayrshiremen a fortnight ago to be ruled out for an earlier infringement by Baur was a low blow.

‘For him, that was a killer,’ O’Neill reflected. ‘He has got the goal, gone off and celebrated and you just think... oh no, is that a goal?

‘He has worked exceptionally hard for us. But strikers live by goals and at some stage or other, he needs a goal.

‘The best thing for me to do is bring Henrik Larsson over and show him how to hit the ball into the net.

‘Shaun Maloney was telling me that for a little period he played up front when Henrik was injured for about a month.

‘And Henrik in that time was giving him advice about how centre-halves were reading him. He told him about getting yourself room, losing the centre-half, don’t be fighting with him all the time.

‘He scored a bag full of goals, so there must be something in it.’

#1432. Juventus sell out Venezia game as Omonia sales pass 35,000

Juventus have sold out Sunday's Serie A home game against Venezia despite a long injury list. Strong early sales for the Europa League visit of Omonia Nicosia keep the club in line for another strong European crowd.

Juventus go into Sunday’s home game against Venezia still short of players. Several remain unavailable for Sunday’s 12:30 kick-off. Edon Zhegrova has trained with the group and is considered available. Celik, Cambiaso, Nico Gonzalez and Kalulu remain out, Sport Mediaset reported. For Spalletti, a full home crowd arrives in the middle of a busy run of games.

General sale for the fixture opened at 3pm on Tuesday 6 October. Supporters living in the province of Venezia could buy only if they held an active Juventus Card. The fixture belongs to the 2026-27 Serie A Enilive season.

This season every Juventus match ticket is digital. Each one is managed through the Allianz Stadium App.

Season-ticket holders who cannot attend can list their seat on resale.juventus.com. The club, not the seller, sets the resale price. A few of those listings are now all that remains for supporters who missed the general sale, ANSA reported.

The season-ticket terms also reward turning up. To keep first refusal on a 2027-28 season ticket, a holder must use the seat for at least 70 per cent of matches. That means at least 13 of the 19 league games.

The Europa League has drawn big numbers to Turin this season. Against NEC, 39,308 match tickets were sold, with away fans counted separately. No away figure was released for the Rennes visit, but that section was full.

The Rennes game finished 2-2 on 22 October. Juventus needed a second-half Woltemade penalty to draw after trailing 2-1.

Omonia Nicosia are next. Bookings for the Cypriot club’s visit still trail the two earlier European crowds.

Juventus have set strict conditions for the fixture. Supporters of Cypriot nationality may buy tickets only for the away section. The club has warned that breaking UEFA rules can lead to cancelled tickets and refused entry.

Taken together, the figures are consistent with a home support that keeps buying despite the injury list. The weekend league fixture will be followed by a European night that is already well on its way to another large crowd.

Juventus host Omonia Nicosia in the Europa League on 26 November.

#1431. Ferrero sets Juventus ambition to be what it once was, as €200m capital raise runs

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he said, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

The new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

The visit showed Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

The financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

The offer involves up to 208.5m new shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment plans.

The spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering new players on its UEFA List A.

Those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

AC Milan have four games left to play in the Europa League and they’re in the do-or-die stage of the competition already.

#1426. Mercato PSG: the strong announcement from Lucas Beraldo’s agent

During the winter of 2024, Paris Saint-Germain put €42 million on the table to afford two young Brazilian talents: Gabriel Moscardo (€20 million) and Lucas Beraldo (€22 million). Almost three years later, the first city has still not had the opportunity to evolve under the orders of Luis Enrique at 21 years old and has a series of loans (Reims, Sporting Braga, Espanyol). As for the second, he remains an understudy in the eyes of the Spanish coach, but has just celebrated, at the age of 22, his 100th match under the red and blue colors. Without forgetting the two Champions Leagues won.

Substitute in Paris, Beraldo is a man of duty who never shy away from the task. Arriving in France as a central defender, the former São Paulo resident has since been tested as a left back and, more recently, a defensive midfielder. A versatility desired by Luis Enrique and valuable for the capital club, but which has not yet been enough to convince Carlo Ancelotti to call him up with Brazil. Not enough to dampen his morale if we are to believe the statements made by his representative, Filipe Tancredi, in the showESPN, Fala a Fonte.

“PSG is betting a lot on him, this is part of a long-term project. Of the 18 matches played, he played 15. He is a very important player in the best team in the world. It’s undeniable. In our eyes, he did an excellent job, and we will end up remembering him in the Brazilian team. Today he plays as a defensive midfielder, but he was trained in central defense and also plays left-back, which is an asset for the Seleção”he declared, before discussing the departure rumors concerning his client.

“He became the youngest Brazilian player to win two Champions Leagues, so he will always attract attention in the market. It is natural that there are many clubs interested and that approaches take place. The likelihood of him leaving PSG… let alone zero, is extremely low. The club is banking heavily on him, and his contract runs until 2031.” The message has gotten through: Lucas Beraldo, who extended his contract last September, has no intention of leaving the capital any time soon!

#1425. Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof

Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Plans to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D

However, the Championship leaders finally turned up in the second half and pulled a goal back through Mohamadou Kanté before Konstantinos Mavropanos equalised with just 10 minutes to go.

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

Tierney did, though, brandish a red card when Kanté pulled back Kyrell Lisbie as the substitute robbed him of the ball on the halfway line and ran clean through on goal.

The foul denied Lisbie the chance to hand Millwall their first win over their bitter rivals for 22 years, much to the frustration of fans who had roared them on from first whistle to last.

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs

Describing the atmosphere as “absolutely the best by far” since he joined the club almost two years ago, Neil said: “I told the players prior to the game that this game’s a real rarity and, as a player and as a manager, it’s a privilege to be part of it.”

Millwall: Marschall; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Sturge; Metcalfe (Servais 81), Mazou-Sacko (Cundle 90); Sykes (Baggott 70), Dykes, Neghli; Arconte (Lisbie 81).Booked: Lisbie 90+5.Goals: Taylor 16, Neghli 45+3.Subs not used: Batth, Crocombe, Doughty, Issoufou, Kelly.West Ham United: Hermansen; Walker-Peters (Kanté 46), Mavropanos, Kilman, Morato; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa (Austbo 68), Solomon; Piroe (Pablo 46), Castellanos (Orford 90).Booked: Morato 40, Pablo 83, Kilman 86, Mavropanos 90+5.Sent off: Kanté 89.Goals: Kanté 74, Mavropanos 80.Subs not used: Ajala, Austbo, Golambeckis, Herrick, Magassa, Scarles.Referee: Paul Tierney.

🗣️ "We started to tire in the second half"Millwall manager Alex Neil shares his thoughts on this afternoon's Dockers Derby, after the Lions drew 2-2 with West Ham. pic.twitter.com/xnmubZ9NIz

🗣️ 'We were able to bounce back, but we need to look at the things we have not done so well'Nuno Espirito Santo reflects on West Ham's performance after the Hammers fought back from 2-0 down to draw with Millwall. pic.twitter.com/NM1wQVcN0o

Asked by Sky Sports for his view on the “spitting” incident, Alex Neil said: “Fil [Marschall] was saying to the referee throughout the game when that happened at that point... Obviously I’m so far away it’s hard for me to see what happened, but I wouldn’t presume that Fil would say that without cause.

“I’m sure the referee and authorities who need to deal with it will look at it and, if it warrants it, it needs dealt with and then I’m sure they will.”

"It's one of the best atmospheres I've ever played in..I got shivers walking out"Millwall's Caleb Taylor speaks to Aaron Paul following today's 2-2 draw with West Ham. pic.twitter.com/yFoRuxooe6

Will there be one final chance? Sturge earns a throw-in on the far side and Dykes limbers up... But West Ham clear their lines and that is that. It ends two goals apiece.

Lisbie has looked dangerous down that left side and he just runs out of room under pressure from Mavropanos. The pair square up, with Lisbie sticking his finger into the Greek’s cheek.

Lisbie darts to the by-line but his cutback does not make it through the thicket of limbs and West Ham clear their lines.

Millwall earn a free-kick to the left of the box as Mavropanos climbs all over Dykes. Servais picks out Baggott at the far post and his knock-down lands to Dykes who, will spinning, strikes the ball over the bar.

DYKES! 😱So close to a late winner for Millwall, but his shot flies over the bar. pic.twitter.com/fQFpQBdS7j

Neghli steps up to take it but it strikes the wall.

There will be five minutes of time added on...

Woah.. Kante gets his pocket picked by Lisbie on the half-way line and the West Ham goalscorer has no choice but to foul him as the last man. West Ham have a free-kick just outside the box.

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs

Millwall have put so much into this and it’s starting to tell. Their players look leggy and aren’t able to track Kante’s run into the channel though Cooper is just about able to clear his lines. Bowen’s corner comes to nothing.

Pablo’s at it again, steaming his way into the left half-space, but Mazou-Sacko does well to track back and block the Brazilian’s effort. The resulting corner is gathered by Marschall who attempts to send Servais away but Kilman is wise to it and takes a booking for a professional foul.

Mazou-Sacko has his hands all over Pablo’s back and while the Brazilian is awarded a free-kick he slams the ball to the ground feeling he had broken free. He earns a booking for his troubles and the resulting free-kick comes to nothing.

Millwall 2 West Ham 2 (Mavropanos) Millwall are finally undone by a cross. Bowen goes short with a corner and Solomon dinks the ball on to the Greek defender’s head and he plants the ball past Marschall. The away end erupts...

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT

It’s Bowen’s turn to try an effort at goal. Metcalfe does brilliantly to charge it down but there is no respite for Millwall as Kante’s long-range sighter goes behind for another corner.

That goal has changed the dynamic of this match. Millwall have dropped into a back five and West Ham are all over them. Bowen earns his side a corner and his delivery comes out to Solomon on the edge of the box, and while Cooper is able to partially clear, Austbo stings the gloves of Marschall from distance to win another corner.

Millwall 2 West Ham 1 (Kante) The substitute strokes a right-footed effort into the bottom corner from outside the box. A great finish.

GOAL for West Ham!Kante finds the back of the net with a clinical finish from outside the box.Can the Hammers draw level? pic.twitter.com/0RZO8oqrtR

Bowen hangs up a corner but Millwall clear their lines with ease. The hosts look so comfortable defending balls into the box.

The versatile defender Baggott is on for Sykes. ITV have just shown a replay of the “spitting” incident but it’s really difficult to make anything out from that distance.

The resulting corner comes to nothing. ITV are relaying reports of a counter-claim from Millwall that Castellanos might have spat in Marschall’s direction.

Chance! Bowen stands up a delightful cross and Pablo forces Marschall into a fine stop. Corner awarded.

Some confusion here as Marschall appears to have taken too long over a goal-kick, and while most believe that a West Ham corner had been awarded, it ends up being a goal-kick.

The ITV commentators say that West Ham are alleging that Marschall spat in Pablo’s direction.

Arconte chases down a lost cause and telescopes a leg through Taylor to earn a corner. He spins around to the home supporters and windmills his arms in their direction as the volume increases. Metcalfe’s cross is well overhit, though, and sails out for a goal-kick.

Kante’s runs in behind are threatening to disrupt Millwall’s backline shape, but Neil’s midfield sentries Mazou-Sacko and Metcalfe are doing such a great job to cover the gaps that the hosts still look like they have things under control.

A thunderous chant of “Milllllllll” echoes around the ground as the home fans spur their charges on.

Oof. Metcalfe leaves a foot in on Morato, his studs going into the defender’s Achilles. He should perhaps consider himself lucky to avoid punishment there. One that VAR may have intervened on in the Premier League.

Penalty shout! Metcalfe drives forward into the right of the box and Kante, who is hot pursuit, pushes the midfielder to the ground. Tierney immediately waves away the appeals and replays concur that the contact is probably not strong enough to warrant a penalty.

Bowen is presented with some grass to run into but his cross is well cleared. He gets another bite at the cherry, trying his luck from the edge of the box and Marschall just about gets to the rebound ahead of an onrushing Kante. A corner is awarded which the Millwall stopper flaps at but his team-mates are able to avert the danger.

West Ham earn a chance to deliver a corner from the near side but Engel’s inswinger finds Marschall’s gloves. Really poor.

Millwall continue leveraging Cooper and Taylor’s height in the box off set-pieces. Here, Metcalfe’s free-kick skims off the top of Cooper’s head but just misses the mark.

It looks like West Ham have gone to three at the back as Kante joins Mukasa and Engels in midfield. He’ll look to make late runs in behind.

Entering the West Ham box, he attempts to hold off Cooper but Osei-Tutu snaps in and earns a free-kick.

Two changes from Nuno, who takes off Piroe and Walker-Peters for Pablo and Kante.

Millwall have been good value for their lead, taking 16 shots and creating three big chances. West Ham, conversely have managed just one shot, off-target, despite controlling two-thirds of possession.

Arne Engel’s heatmap suggests he’s spent most of the match inside or just in advance of West Ham’s defensive third, which is not where Nuno will want either him or Divine Mukasa. The West Ham head coach could be tempted into changes at the break.

This is no more than Millwall – and West Ham – deserve. Sykes’s outrageous 35-yard strike deserved a goal and Neghli makes sure justice is served on the stroke of half-time. The roar that greets the players leaving the field is deafening.

The Den is in dreamland. Millwall take a two-goal advantage into the break and Neil celebrates with unbridled delight on the touchline. A caveat, though... Millwall did spurn a 2-0 lead in their most recent match away at Middlesbrough.

Millwall 2 West Ham 0 (Neghli) It’s come from yet another Dykes long throw, which West Ham have failed to clear. The ball falls to the feet of Neghli in the six-yard box and he spears the ball beyond Hermansen and Bowen on the line. And that’s the half.

"It's DREAMLAND at the Den!!"🫶🏼Millwall snatch a second goal before the break, as Neghli drills it home.An unbelievable half from the home side. pic.twitter.com/NIfSmwkHXh

Chance! Sykes from 30 yards strikes the ball cleanly and his ferocious effort beats Hermansen all ends up but ricochets off the woodwork and away to safety. Two minutes of time added on, by the way...

WHAT A HIT!! 💥Sykes' long-range effort RATTLES the crossbar. A potential contender for goal of the season, had that gone into the net... pic.twitter.com/ivBOslIZaO

Millwall, for the umpteenth time, find themselves in a two-vs-two situation on the beak, as Arconte tries to twist Kilman one way and then the other. He sets the ball to Metcalfe but the contact is not great and Hermansen gathers.

West Ham threaten Millwall’s lead momentarily as Mukasa breaks down their right, but Marschall does well to smother the ball and earns a free-kick on the process.

There’s a muted appeal for a penalty as Mavropanos nudges Cooper to the floor, but it’s a soft contact which takes place outside of the box anyhow.

Castellanos then attempts to burst down the right but Mazou-Sacko, who has been fantastic thus far, steams in and boots the ball out of play before geeing up the crowd.

Another foul... Osei-Tutu jumps into Morato but West Ham give the free-kick straight back to their opponents.

Morato leaves a leg in as Osei-Tutu attempts to break free, perhaps in retaliation to the earlier discretion, and he earns the first booking of the match.

It’s seven-seven in the fouls contest for those wondering, the latest being a mistimed challenge on Sykes by Castellanos near the right touchline. Millwall pump another ball into the box which is not up to much.

In an attempt to get his foot on the ball, Engels has often peeled out to the right-back position, but a wild, desperate cross-field ball that goes straight to Osei-Tutu sums up West Ham’s half aptly.

A wild challenge from Metcalfe on Cooper earns West Ham a free-kick and its then Sykes’ turn to land a late tackle, this time in the right channel. The subsequent delivery finds Castellanos but he cannot direct the ball goalwards.

West Ham’s strength comes from the fluidity of their front four, but Nuno’s creators have not been able to access them. So effective has Millwall’s back-line coverage been that West Ham have only managed low-quality final-third entries.

For the first time this half, Millwall begin to retreat deep into their own half, their lines of defence merging. And while West Ham tot up a fair number of passes on the edge of the box, they ultimately cede possession and Millwall spring a counter. Arconte appears to be through but Kilman does well to recover and Dykes’ subsequent shot is charged down.

West Ham are not learning their lessons and Sturge almost pulls off a similar pass in behind for Arconte, but the linesman raises his flag on this occasion. Replays show that it was really tight.

Millwall are going man-to-man as West Ham try to build and the visitors are struggling to get out. Sturge works infield from his starting perch on the left and almost threads a through-ball in behind for Arconte to gallop on to but Kilman does well to stick in a boot.

West Ham are desperately trying to calm this game down, but the Millwall fans are making that quite the challenge. The visitors string a series of passes together before Bowen strays offside.

Millwall then burst forward, Arconte this time popping up in a dangerous position on the right but Metcalfe fires over having picked off a loose Hammers pass out from the back.

Another Dykes throw-in sparks panic in West Ham’s box. Osei-Tutu’s back-post header appears to take a deflection off Walker-Peters, but the referee awards a goal-kick.

Millwall 1 West Ham 0 (Taylor) If at first you don’t succeed, try and try again... Dykes’ long throw from the right prompts chaos on the West Ham box and although Hermansen is able to keep out efforts from Sykes and Arconte, he can’t deny Taylor from close range. Cue bedlam in the stands. A massive, massive goal.

Or not… The Den erupts! That was appalling defending from a long throw and West Ham got exactly what they deserved, with Mads Hemansen’s brilliant save failing to spare them.

MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D

It is all Millwall so far. They have been first to pretty much every ball and are giving West Ham no time on it at all. Konstantinos Mavropanos has just bought the visitors a breather after going down injured.

Hermansen gets caught in no-man’s land as Millwall spin in another ball from deep. It falls to the feet of Dykes but his effort does not have the requisite power to beat Kilman on the line.

Mavropanos appears to have been taken out by his own goalkeeper in the commotion and receives some on-field medical treatment.

Neil will be happy with how his side have started this match. Their intensity off the ball has forced West Ham into errors and here Sturge picks Bowen’s pocket on the halfway line before picking out Arconte in the box. He tries to squeeze a shot through Mukasa but the young midfielder does well to clear his lines.

The resulting corner comes out to Mazou-Sacko on the edge of the box but his effort sails over the bar.

Dykes and Arconte are Millwall’s attacking threats and the former wins a free-kick in the left channel. The hosts load the box with their biggest aerial threats but Metcalfe’s teasing inswinger just evades everyone. Tierney blows up for a foul anyhow...

There’s a minor clash off the ball as Morato and Cooper exchange words. Paul Tierney speaks with both players before Dykes launches a long throw into the box which is cleared and Hermansen is wise to the subsequent cross off the second phase.

Arconte tiptoes into the West Ham box and picks out Sturge whose miscued shot finds Metcalfe on the edge of the box. His effort is straight at Hermansen who collects the ball calmly.

That Jenson Metcalfe tackle on West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen came after just 15 seconds. What Vinny Jones might call “a reducer”.

"That's the expectation, I would imagine" 😅The first free-kick is awarded just 12 seconds into Millwall's derby against West Ham.Watch it LIVE on ITV1 🎥 pic.twitter.com/qpxjQEKN6x

Millwall launch a free-kick from deep into the box after Castellanos gives away a needless foul and after some pinball Hermansen gathers.

It took just 13 seconds for us to get our first foul. Kudos to anyone who had that in their Dockers Derby sweepstake... A late lunge from Metcalfe on Bowen.

And the players emerge, Hey Jude now being played... Millwall are in their customary navy-blue home strip and white shorts. West Ham are giving their new white away kit a first outing.

There’s just about enough time for the two sides to meet for quick summits before Millwall get us under way!

The atmosphere is building nicely in the ground and the players are now lined up in the tunnel, Cooper and Bowen standing shoulder to shoulder.

Seats are filling up rapidly with barely 10 minutes before kick-off, with the away end a notable exception. The home fans are making their own presence felt as The Jam’s A Town Called Malice and The Clash’s London Calling blare out over the public-address system.

"The fans are up for it, the players are up for it" 💪🏼Lyndon Dykes looks ahead to today's match, and reflects on his strong start to life as a Millwall player.Watch it LIVE on ITV1 🎥 pic.twitter.com/V9nPzbh3Ob

Kevin Nolan, West Ham’s captain, was sent off early but his team-mates defied the odds to win 2-1 thanks to goals from Carlton Cole and Winston Reid either side of a stunning Liam Trotter strike.

In Millwall’s match-day squad that day were… Harry Kane and Ryan Mason.

The last time West Ham and Millwall met, Harry Kane was a Millwall player 😅This is how that game in 2012 played out 👇 pic.twitter.com/OhtVx3caCP

This rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

“There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” says Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”

Though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

“It really is about the hooligan era,” says a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”

Jake Cooper on making the 500th appearance of his career against West Ham today! 👏Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/lTzXOwXhxd

There have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

At the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at New Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

The hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

Mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police said that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

Just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means…

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

When asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno said: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [important], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

On potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”

The gaffer on tomorrow's fixture ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/6NG6t4t4Fn

#westham on the way to #millwall via #london bridge #whufc #coyi pic.twitter.com/HrWgJ6UtJY

Riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

The game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

The Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

Alex Neil switches out goalkeeper Max Crocombe for Filip Marschall and names the returning Mathis Servais, Kyrell Lisbie and Alfie Doughty on the bench.

Alex Neil names his Lions XI 👊 pic.twitter.com/MP0N9wMatG

Just the one change from the league leaders’ last league match as Kyle Walker-Peters comes in for the injured Joel Veltman.

Today's teamsheet 📋 pic.twitter.com/EmrxYRhsPd

"We have to quiet them down" 🤫West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen is expecting a hostile atmosphere at The Den today 🗣️Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/9tp2225Rq8

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

Acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

Both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

Since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

Much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

#1423. Camarda recalls emotion of disallowed UCL goal and Gabbia’s words: “I burst into tears”

Francesco Camarda has spoken about his Champions League goal that never was today, and how it was an AC Milan dream come true.

Camarda first became known to Milan as a youngster, but he announced himself further when he became Serie A’s youngest-ever appearance maker. He almost then went to a European level, with a goal in the Champions League. However, it wasn’t to be.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

On his debut in the competition, the starlet bagged a goal which would’ve made him the Rossoneri’s youngest-ever scorer in Europe’s main stage. Yet it was ruled out for offside and a few years on, the now 18-year-old is still waiting for a first competitive goal for the Diavolo.

Speaking to Vice, the striker opened up about his dream of playing in the Champions League at San Siro, his emotions after his goal (and it later being disallowed) and how his teammates rallied around him, as MilanVibes relayed.

“As a child, I used to say to my dad: imagine if one day I could walk into San Siro and hear the Champions League anthem, accompanied by the roar of the entire stadium. When it actually happened, I thought back to that little boy and realised I had realised a dream.

“When I stepped onto the pitch, I had an incredible adrenaline rush. Then the goal came, and I felt the whole stadium explode. I also felt the affection of my teammates, who immediately raised me into the air.

“However, when I looked at the scoreboard and saw that the VAR check was in progress, I was already convinced the goal would be disallowed.

“When I returned home that evening, with my parents and cousin, I burst into tears. I was overjoyed by the goal, but at the same time deeply disappointed by what had happened. It wasn’t easy at first, but I also worked on my mental health and managed to put that moment behind me.

“Today, I’m proud of the journey I’ve taken and of having overcome those difficulties.”

“I remember what Gabbia told me: he was sorry for what happened, but he explained that the experience should give me even more motivation. It should push me to improve, to train harder, and to work so I can relive even more wonderful emotions.”

“In football, there are positive and negative opinions; it has always been this way and will continue to be this way. A player’s true strength lies in not being influenced by what is said, because, regardless of whether you do well or badly, someone will always find a reason to judge you.”

#1421. CAN 2025: Senegal-Morocco, huge drama after the CAS verdict!

The series of the CAN 2025 final is not yet over. A few hours after the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which confirmed Senegal’s victory against Morocco, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) officially reacted. In a particularly firm statement, the Moroccan body expressed its disagreement with this decision and announced its intention to initiate new legal procedures.

“The Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its protest against the fact that its request was not taken into consideration”indicates in particular the press release published this Tuesday. The FRMF considers that its arguments concerning the alleged irregularities of the procedure have not been sufficiently examined by the sports court. It considers in particular that certain elements call into question “the integrity and credibility of the decision. »

To support its protest, the FRMF highlights a specific element: “It was confirmed that contact had taken place between the German referee, Ulrich Haas, and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was given. » The Moroccan Federation believes that this situation should have been taken into consideration when examining the file.

The Moroccan body also contests the interpretation adopted by the CAS concerning the temporary departure of the Senegalese players from the field during the final. She believes that the decision “still does not take into account the need to comply with the direction enshrined in recent decisions of the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA). »

The FRMF particularly emphasizes the regulatory consequences of the behavior of players who leave the field without the authorization of the referee. She thus evokes “the resulting responsibilities and disciplinary sanctions”considering that this aspect was not correctly taken into account in the decision rendered in Lausanne.

Despite the CAS verdict, the Moroccan Federation does not intend to turn the page. She clearly announced her desire to continue the process: “As a result, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation has decided to initiate all necessary legal procedures to challenge the CAS decision. »

As a reminder, the Court of Arbitration for Sport annulled the decision of the CAF Appeal Jury, which had awarded a victory on the green carpet to Morocco (3-0). He reinstated the decision of the Disciplinary Jury and confirmed the result obtained on the field, a victory for Senegal (1-0). The reaction of the FRMF now opens a new sequence in this particularly tense issue between the two federations.

#1420. Montella describes ‘dream’ Milan opportunity, Berlusconi and the Supercoppa: “An incredible feeling”

Vincenzo Montella’s time with AC Milan was ‘a dream’ for him, but he failed to achieve much during his time at the helm.

Looking back on Montella’s time leading Milan is tricky. On paper, the Italian had a strong tenure at the club, achieving a 50% win rate and only losing 18 of his 64 games in charge at San Siro, not a terrible record by any means.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He even ended a five-year trophy drought with a win against Juventus in the Supercoppa Italiana and returned the Rossoneri to Europe, with a sixth-place finish in the 2016/17 season. In itself, that was a first since 2014.

This is where context matters, though. The start of the 2017/18 season was tough, as the Diavolo won six of their first 14 games and he was sacked before December. Despite that, he still views the club in an excellent light.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport’s ‘La Tripletta’ podcast, Montella went over his time with the club and how he fulfilled a dream by taking the job, as MilanPress relays.

“It was a fantastic experience there [at Milan] too, it was my dream. Then, as a professional, it’s a little different, but when I was thirteen I was a fan of that AC Milan team. My older brother took me to see Maradona’s Napoli team twice to make me a Napoli fan, and Maradona scored three goals.

“Despite this, my idol was Van Basten because I was a striker: I studied him and dreamed of becoming like him, and so I was a Milan fan. I knew everything about Milan, so for me it was an incredible feeling to join Milan.”

“He liked to talk about football; he liked to give advice even when it was a bit out of context at the time, because he always had the mentality of having Van Basten as a centre forward with Papin, a two-time Ballon d’Or winner, on the bench. He wanted me to play with two strikers, and I tried to plug the gap for months.

“I told him it was difficult; I knew all the lineups of those years. I was a Milan fan: the starter was Van Basten and the reserve was Papin, both Ballon d’Or winners. So, ‘If you buy me some players like that, rest assured that I’ll play them both.'”

“It was a year when we returned to Europe. I think it had been two or three years since Milan had been there, and it was something new at the time. We won a trophy, a small one. Just the other night I saw Galliani at a dinner; he reminded me of it and remembers it perfectly.

“I have to say that I found him to be the perfect manager at the time, because he was always on my side when it came to pressure; he gave me complete autonomy in my decisions and he helped me with everything, from the number of collaborators to new things; whatever I asked for, he was always on the coach’s side.

“And so for me he was truly an incredible manager, who in that phase, in that change, was fundamental even in achieving these small results, especially after Berlusconi’s great AC Milan.

“We deserved to win even in regulation time: we had some easy chances to win it, then it came to penalties. Gigio saved the penalty from Dybala, who kicked it really hard, but he filled the net with it.”

“I was a little worried from the beginning because there was this obsession with publicising everything, almost like a publicity stunt, so I was a little worried. In theory, there was sharing, at least that’s what it looked like, but I couldn’t back out when in reality that wasn’t always the case.

“And so sometimes there were players I hadn’t even consulted about, who would arrive and then say, ‘It was shared,’ and when you’re there, you can’t say otherwise. Certainly, when you build a team and have the budget, the first thing you do is: we had a goalkeeper, I’ll get a centre forward, we were missing a centre forward.

“In the final selection, the centre forward was the only one left, with a budget of 15-20 million. And then Kalinic… yes, I chose him because that was the final budget. So our, let’s say, second-choice striker was paid thirty-eight million, if I remember correctly, who was André Silva, and the first striker was paid half that.

“And so, in my opinion, a misunderstanding of this kind was created, with so many changes, even though at that stage we weren’t even playing badly for having fifteen new players.

“We still had Calhanoglu, who wasn’t feeling well, coming off months of suspension. The team was still being built: we weren’t in line with the Scudetto objectives that had been announced, but certainly, given our development, we were absolutely on target.

“Who would I have signed up front? At the time, we were probably negotiating for Aubameyang, if I remember correctly. Ronaldo? No, I didn’t believe it, not at all.”

#1418. A footballer who loves getting cards! Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo opens up on his passion for collecting as he launches trading card shop in London with Chelsea's Reece James and Levi Colwill

Published: 18:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:06 EST, 20 November 2026

Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.

Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.

Adarabioyo began collecting as a child and returned to the hobby in 2020. His collection, which he shares on social media, spans a variety of sports and he also has several of Brazilian icon Neymar.

'I’ve been collecting for years, and it’s great to see the hobby continue to grow,' said the 29-year-old, who left Chelsea for Spurs last summer.

'I love collecting. It’s a great way for supporters to connect with their favourite players. I’ve always felt that collectors are some of the most passionate fans.

'I’ve got to know so many collectors through the hobby. Talking about our collections is an instant icebreaker, and I know those conversations can mean a lot. I want to bring more players into the hobby and recreate those moments.

Tosin Adarabioyo, like many footballers, has a passion for collecting trading cards

The new shop is set to open in London's Borough Market next week

Adarabioyo enjoyes collecting cards of former PSG star Neymar, who won 130 caps for Brazil

'Neymar is criminally underrated to me, and I think his cards are too. Some of the images take me straight back to performances I’ve watched over the years. It’s hard to describe, but it’s like bottling up that feeling forever. Football purists will know what I mean.'

West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters, who played with Tosin at England youth level, is among backers along with James and Colwill.

Adarabioyo already has an online retail business, The Huddle, with guests such as Dominic Solanke, Robert Sanchez and Adam Wharton all featuring on live streams, opening boxes as fans watch.

Recent figures valued the global sports trading card market at $13.75billion (£10.5bn) in 2025, with that projected to grow to $27.52bn (£21bn) by 2034.

Formula One star Lewis Hamilton got in on the act earlier this year, launching his own venture and a shop in Frankfurt.

The seven-time world champion was already an ambassador for Topps - who also have the licence for Premier League cards - and said: 'I’ve loved collecting cards since I was a kid — Pokemon, football, anything I could get my hands on.

'To now play a role in shaping the future of the category is incredible. We have a significant opportunity to tap into the culture in a way no one has before.'

#1417. How Amorim picked apart Alvini’s gung-ho approach: Tactical analysis of AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone

AC Milan put on arguably their best display of the Ruben Amorim era so far as they beat Frosinone 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.

Gabriele Calvani’s early own-goal kicked off what would be a miserable night for the Canarini, before Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. Patrizio Masini’s goal halved the deficit, and kept the game open going into the second half.

From there, though, the Rossoneri ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both scored within minutes of coming off the bench, finishing counter-attacks, then Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed to move back into the top four, also given that only Inter out of the top six sides in the table dropped points. Rohit Rajeev has the tactical breakdown from the win.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Milan once again deployed a modified version of their 3-4-2-1, with Bartesaghi operating on the left. Alvini, meanwhile, had to cope without his striker Raimondo and opted for a 3-5-2, pairing Ghedjemis and Kvernadze up front.

Frosinone made their intentions clear from the opening seconds. Goalkeeper Palmisani immediately played a direct ball into a targeted zone, with Frosinone committing several players towards the expected landing area to create a numerical advantage and win the aerial duel.

Milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper.

Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive.

This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper. Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive. However, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up. Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

— Rohit Rajeev (@keralista) November 23, 2026

However, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up.

Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

This movement directly contributed to Milan’s opening goal. Rabiot dropped between the lines to receive possession, forcing Cittadini to step out of his defensive position and follow him.

Rabiot then laid the ball off to Modric, who immediately played it into the space vacated by Cittadini. Under pressure, Frosinone inadvertently turned the ball into their own net to give Milan a 1-0 lead.

Frosinone looked to commit numbers into Milan’s half, creating ball-sided overloads to progress through the pitch. Their two wingers maintained wide positions to stretch Milan’s wing-backs and create more space in the central areas.

Out of possession, Frosinone adopted a 3-4-3 to match Milan’s 3-4-2-1 in possession. They also maintained a very high defensive line, looking to press Milan aggressively and win the ball back as high up the pitch as possible.

Milan allowed Frosinone to dictate possession, dropping into a deeper defensive block to invite them into their half. Once Frosinone advanced, Milan looked to win the ball back and launch quick counter-attacks.

Frosinone’s lack of a clear attacking structure and, more importantly, an organised rest defence left them vulnerable in transition. Milan exploited this disorganisation repeatedly, with the next four goals all benefiting from the spaces Frosinone left behind.

The second goal perfectly illustrated Milan’s approach in transition. Frosinone had committed ten players into Milan’s half, leaving very little defensive cover behind.

Ramos won possession, and Musah immediately played a vertical pass to release Moreira through on goal. Moreira and Rabiot then drew three recovering defenders towards them before creating the space for Ramos to finish.

Frosinone’s high-risk approach briefly paid off with Masini’s goal. They drew Milan into central areas before pressing aggressively to recover possession. With their players positioned close together, they were able to combine quickly and progress the ball towards Kvernadze.

A deflection off De Winter then took the ball into Ghedjemis’ path, allowing him to set up Masini for the finish.

Frosinone consistently targeted Milan’s left flank, particularly the space around Bartesaghi. The individual duel between Ghedjemis and Bartesaghi became a key feature of the game.

Ghedjemis repeatedly beat his marker in 1v1 situations and posed a threat. Recognising the problem, Amorim took Bartesaghi off at half-time.

After the break, Jashari and Pulisic began making coordinated counter-movements. Pulisic dropped deeper, drawing his marker away and creating space in the wide attacking area, which Jashari then exploited with an advancing run.

The goal was very similar to the movement Jashari made against Venezia, highlighting a recurring pattern in Milan’s attacking play.

Both Cisse’s and Pulisic’s goals came from a counter-attack following a Frosinone corner, for which they did not leave many men back.

For Cisse’s finish, his body orientation suggested he was going to shoot towards the goalkeeper’s right, prompting the keeper to adjust his stance accordingly. Cisse then went the other way, finding the opposite corner.

⚽️ GOAL ALPHADJO CISSE! 🔥 https://t.co/aMIgE9PXHc

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

Pulisic, meanwhile, used the bridge of his foot to execute a delicate chip, lifting the ball over the advancing goalkeeper and completing the counter-attack.

⚽️ GOAL CHRISTIAN PULISIC 🇺🇸 https://t.co/B4mP55RJ8u

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

We wrote something during the break about how Milan are over-performing relative to certain metrics. Above all, their actual goals scored was/is well above their Expected Goals, helped by the fact four players are converting an abnormally high percentage of chances.

With this in mind, the stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals, so they again out-performed what they created. And yet, the Rossoneri racked up five big chances which matches the number of goals scored.

So, perhaps everything can be taken with a pinch of whatever type of salt fits your narrative. Many would argue that Milan could have scored more given their brilliant on Sunday, yet xG would have you believe it was a ‘lucky’ margin in a game that should have been 2/3-1.

The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season, but thankfully Amorim’s side managed to deal with them all relatively well.

#1416. No bans after matchday 12: Juventus and Como at full strength for the Sinigaglia

The Serie A disciplinary judge suspended no players after matchday 12, so neither Juventus nor Como lose anyone for Sunday's game. Como were fined again for a slow restart, and Juventus head to Lake Como five points behind them.

Juventus travel to Como on Sunday with no suspension worries. Nor do their hosts. Serie A disciplinary judge Gerardo Mastrandrea banned nobody after matchday 12 in a ruling published in Milan on 24 November.

The decisions covered the games of 21, 22 and 23 November. Nobody was sent off across the round. No player one booking from a ban picked up a yellow card either.

Juventus had no cards from their own fixture. The club’s match sheet for the 4-0 win over Venezia at the Allianz Stadium lists no bookings, with Arena as referee.

All four goals came after the break. Woltemade (53′), Koopmeiners (59′) and Cabal (65′) scored before Kolo Muani converted a penalty (71′).

The list of players one caution from suspension is now short. Only two names remain, both from Lecce, each on a fourth booking, Virgilio Sport reported. Neither club meeting on Sunday has a player in that position.

Como did not escape the judge entirely. The fine was imposed under strict liability for a delay without good reason. The judge treated it as a repeated repeat offence.

It was the largest of the round’s penalties for late restarts. Fiorentina and Milan were also fined as repeat offenders. Genoa received €3,000 for a two-minute delay to kick-off.

The problem is not new for Como. In the previous round, the communiqué of 10 November fined them €10,000, again as repeated repeat offenders. On that occasion the second half started about two minutes late.

Juventus were not blameless that week. The same 10 November ruling fined them €5,000 for holding up the start of the first half by the same margin as Como’s latest delay.

The match carries weight in the race for the top four. Como have 8 wins, 2 draws and 2 defeats from their 12 games. They have scored 20 goals and conceded 10.

Juventus have 6 wins, 3 draws and 3 defeats. Their attack, with 19 goals, has almost kept pace with Como’s. The difference lies at the back, where Juventus have conceded 12.

A win on Lake Como would narrow the gap to their hosts. Defeat would push Juventus further from the top four.

Como host Juventus at the Sinigaglia on 29 November.
